▪︎PE (dorsal lithotomy): soft, smooth mass protruding from genital hiatus, ⇡ w/ Valsalva; may leak urine w/ cough
▪︎cystocele: smooth mass w/ vaginal rugae from anterior vaginal wall (= bladder pushing the wall) → ⍉bx
▪︎rectocele: smooth mass w/ vaginal rugae from posterior vaginal wall; rectovaginal palpation (septal thinning); DRE confirms sacculation into vagina
▪︎POP-Q (anterior): Aa = 3cm proximal to urethral meatus (−3 to +3); Ba = most distal point of upper anterior wall; measured vs hymen during max Valsalva; stage 0 (⍉prolapse) → IV (complete eversion)

▪︎pessary if concern for tissue ulceration or bothersome sx; ring pessary MC 1st-line; needs ongoing maintenance
▪︎PFMT (Kegel): may improve sx + slow progression; for urinary incont w/ cystocele
▪︎topical vaginal estrogen for atrophic tissue optimization

▪︎surg = definitive tx; reserved for severe cases or ulceration/tissue destruction
▪︎cystocele: anterior colporrhaphy (native tissue; midline plication of pubocervical fascia) = 1st-line surg repair; ⇡anatomic recurrence
▪︎mesh-augmented repair: ⇣recurrence but ⇡mesh exposure, chronic pain, reoperation (FDA restrictions in US)
▪︎paravaginal repair: reattaches lat vaginal fascia to ATFP (isolated paravaginal defect dx by exam = unreliable)
▪︎concurrent apical suspension = critical (most anterior prolapse has an apical component; ⇣recurrence)

▪︎occult SUI: prolapse can kink urethra + mask SUI; ~40% of continent pts develop SUI after repair w/o anti-incont procedure → preop cough stress test w/ prolapse reduced (300mL bladder vol); consider midurethral sling or Burch if OSUI
▪︎rectocele: tx constipation (high-fiber diet), pessary, surg if conservative fails; definitive = posterior colporrhaphy
*Preg women may present w/ new sxs or an exacerbation of prolapse – managed conservatively
